content.text:
Before 9832217, `sourceTrack.getTimes()` would NPE if there was no source track (null) — so the "fix" in 9832217 avoided the crash by skipping the track entirely. That's exactly the bug the HEAD commit fixes: mapped target bones with no source track got no track at all (losing bind-pose/mapping influence), instead of a proper single-keyframe bind-pose track. This confirms 9832217 is the bug's origin, not a pre-existing crash-fix without issue — it merely traded a crash for silently-missing bones.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 98322172593acecf02869258c392cc4d08155fb1

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the history of `src/main/java/maud/Util.java` with `git log -p --follow`, specifically searching for the `if (sourceTrack != null)` pattern that was removed in the fix commit 7a91a35. This surfaced two prior commits touching that exact code path: `9832217` (introduced the guard) and `fe2ccb8` (merely added an explanatory comment `// handle null sourceTrack` to the existing guard, no logic change).

**(2) Specific change:** Commit `9832217` refactored `retargetAnimation`/`retargetTrack`: it moved the `MyAnimation.findTrack(...)` lookup out of `retargetTrack` and into the caller, then wrapped the call to `retargetTrack` + `result.addTrack(track)` in `if (sourceTrack != null) { ... }`. This made the method silently skip adding any track for a target bone whose mapped source bone has no animation track — rather than producing a sensible bind-pose track for it. The HEAD fix commit reverses exactly this: it removes the `if (sourceTrack != null)` guard so a track is *always* added, and pushes null-handling into `retargetTrack` itself (synthesizing a single-keyframe bind-pose track when `sourceTrack == null`).

**(3) Supporting evidence:** Examining the parent of `9832217` (`git show 9832217^:...Util.java`) shows the pre-existing code unconditionally called `retargetTrack`, which itself called `sourceTrack.getTimes()` without a null check — meaning a null source track would have thrown an NPE. Commit `9832217` avoided that crash but introduced the actual bug (silently dropping bones from the retargeted animation instead of giving them a bind-pose track). `fe2ccb8` only added a clarifying comment to the already-buggy guard, confirming it did not alter behavior. The HEAD commit's diff directly undoes `9832217`'s guard and implements the correct null-handling that should have been there from the start.

I'm fairly confident in this attribution since the removed code block in the fix is textually identical (modulo the comment) to what `9832217` added, and no other commit in the history touches this logic.
